## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Avivittakathā* (Kv 21.2) is an Abhidhamma debate belonging to the twenty-first chapter of the *Kathāvatthu* [Catalog; SuttaCentral]. As outlined by André Bareau, the discussion centers on the proposition that an ordinary person (*puthujjana*) is not separated or detached (*avivitta*) from the phenomena (*dhamma*) of the threefold world (*tedhātuka*) [Bareau 1955]. The thesis contends that because worldly dhammas are not fully comprehended (*apariññāta*) by an ordinary person, that person is not separated from them; this relates to the principle that phenomena are fixed in their own intrinsic nature (*sabhāva*) and never abandon (*vijahanti*) it, as in the case of material form (*rūpa*) remaining fixed in the nature of form [Bareau 1955].
SuttaCentral notes one translation of the text and lists no historical parallels [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus detects 68 matching Pali passages shared with six texts, predominantly with other Kathāvatthu debates such as the *Jahatikathā* (Kv 1.5), the *Sabbamatthītikathā* (Kv 1.6), the *Asekhañāṇakathā* (Kv 5.2), and the *Anāsavakathā* (Kv 4.3), along with shared formulaic segments with the *Navakanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 9) and the *Visuddhimagga* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records low-scoring automatic alignments with the Tibetan *Vinayapraśnaṭīkā* (D4135) [DharmaNexus].
